_meta.description: RetroDojo emulator reference dataset. Maps emulators to the systems they emulate, their source repositories, graphics API requirements, and platform support. Used by chipsets.html to cross-reference SoC emulation capability with emulator requirements.

speed_scale.full_speed: Sustains target FPS (usually 60) at native resolution consistently across the library.
speed_scale.playable: 30-60fps at native resolution; occasional drops but enjoyable gameplay.
speed_scale.slow: Sub-30fps or frequent stutters; technically runs but frustrating.
speed_scale.not_capable: Cannot run the emulator meaningfully on this SoC.

upscale_scale.3x+: Can render at 3x native resolution or higher.
upscale_scale.1x_only: Native resolution is the performance ceiling.

setup_scale.plug_and_play: Default settings, no per-game tuning needed.
setup_scale.light_config: A few global settings tweaks required.
setup_scale.per_game_tuning: Many titles need individual performance profiles.
setup_scale.heavy_tweaking: Extensive optimization, custom builds, or special drivers needed.

driver_gate_scale.vulkan_preferred: Vulkan improves performance significantly but OpenGL works.
driver_gate_scale.vulkan_required: Vulkan driver quality is the primary bottleneck.
driver_gate_scale.vendor_specific: Only works well on specific vendor drivers (e.g., Qualcomm Adreno for Switch emulation).

emulation_tiers.label: 8-bit & 16-bit
emulation_tiers.notes: Any modern ARM SoC handles these at full speed. Even budget Allwinner/RK chips have no issues. DOS and ScummVM games also fit here.

emulation_tiers.label: PS1 / N64 / Saturn
emulation_tiers.notes: First-gen 3D. PS1 is easy; N64 is deceptively hard due to complex RDP emulation. Saturn depends heavily on emulator maturity.

emulation_tiers.label: PSP / DS / Dreamcast
emulation_tiers.notes: Well-optimized standalone emulators exist. PSP via PPSSPP is remarkably efficient. DS needs dual-screen rendering.

emulation_tiers.label: GameCube / Wii / 3DS
emulation_tiers.notes: Dolphin needs real GPU + Vulkan. 3DS via Azahar/Citra needs decent CPU. This is where SoC tier really starts to matter.

emulation_tiers.label: PS2 / Wii U
emulation_tiers.notes: PS2 via AetherSX2/NetherSX2 needs strong CPU + driver stack. Wii U via Cemu is Android-only recent and demanding.

emulation_tiers.label: Nintendo Switch
emulation_tiers.notes: Yuzu/Eden/Skyline — Qualcomm Adreno Vulkan drivers are practically required on Android. Mali GPUs struggle significantly. x86 platforms (AMD/Intel) have better compatibility via desktop emulators.

emulation_tiers.label: PC Gaming
emulation_tiers.notes: Winlator (Wine + Box86/Box64) translates x86 Windows games to ARM. Only practical on flagship SoCs (SD 8 Gen 2+). DirectX → Vulkan via DXVK. Very demanding.

emulation_tiers.label: Game Streaming
emulation_tiers.notes: Not emulation — depends on Wi-Fi quality, H.265/AV1 hardware decode, and latency. GameNative and GeForce NOW run games server-side; Steam Remote Play streams from your own PC. Higher Wi-Fi standards (Wi-Fi 6/7) significantly improve experience.

emulators.name: RetroArch
emulators.notes: Frontend for libretro cores. Covers most systems up to PSP/Dreamcast tier. Individual core quality varies.

emulators.name: PPSSPP
emulators.notes: Remarkably well-optimized. Runs full speed on most mid-range SoCs. Vulkan backend preferred for best performance.

emulators.name: DuckStation
emulators.notes: High-accuracy PS1 emulator. Supports upscaling, PGXP geometry correction. Very efficient.

emulators.name: Dolphin
emulators.notes: GameCube/Wii. Vulkan is critical for Android performance. Mali GPU Vulkan drivers limit compatibility vs Adreno.

emulators.name: Azahar (Citra fork)
emulators.notes: Community fork of Citra after original was discontinued. Needs decent CPU for full speed.

emulators.name: Citra MMJ
emulators.notes: Android-optimized Citra fork. Often better performance than official builds on handhelds.

emulators.name: AetherSX2 / NetherSX2
emulators.notes: PS2 emulation on Android. AetherSX2 development paused; NetherSX2 patch continues. Vulkan driver quality directly determines game compatibility.

emulators.name: ARMSX2
emulators.notes: Newer PS2 Android emulator. Active development. Requires strong SoC with good Vulkan support.

emulators.name: Flycast
emulators.notes: Well-optimized Dreamcast emulator. Runs well even on mid-range hardware.

emulators.name: MelonDS
emulators.notes: Accurate DS emulator. Dual-screen rendering has moderate CPU cost.

emulators.name: Eden (Yuzu fork)
emulators.notes: Switch emulation on Android. Requires Qualcomm Adreno GPU with up-to-date Vulkan drivers. Mali GPUs have severe compatibility issues. Custom Adreno driver packs (Turnip) significantly improve performance.

emulators.name: Cemu
emulators.notes: Wii U emulator. Android port is relatively new. Demanding on both CPU and GPU.

emulators.name: GameNative
emulators.notes: Cloud-native game streaming service. Runs games server-side — no local GPU needed. Quality depends on Wi-Fi and H.265/AV1 decode.

emulators.name: GeForce NOW
emulators.notes: NVIDIA cloud gaming. Plays your Steam/Epic/Ubisoft library on NVIDIA's servers. Requires subscription for priority access. AV1 decode recommended.

emulators.name: Steam Remote Play
emulators.notes: Streams games from your own PC via Steam. Low latency on local network. Requires a gaming PC running Steam.

emulators.name: Xbox Cloud Gaming
emulators.notes: Microsoft cloud gaming via Game Pass Ultimate. Plays Xbox/PC titles server-side. Browser-based option available.

emulators.name: Moonlight
emulators.notes: Open-source Sunshine/GameStream client. Streams from your own PC. Low-latency alternative to Steam Remote Play.

emulators.name: Winlator
emulators.notes: Runs Windows x86 games on Android via Wine + translation layer. Very demanding. Only practical on flagship SoCs (SD 8 Gen 2+, Dragonwing Q8).

emulators.name: ScummVM
emulators.notes: Re-implementation of classic adventure game engines. Minimal hardware requirements.
